title: Stop-loss approximation for Rademacher sums
statement:
There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every $n$, every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb R^n$ with $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, every $\varepsilon>0$ satisfying $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for all $i$, and every $t\ge0$, the stop-loss expectation of the Rademacher sum $\sum_i a_i x_i$ differs from that of a standard Gaussian by at most $C\varepsilon$:
\[\left|\mathbb E_x\left(\sum_i a_i x_i-t\right)^+-\int_{\mathbb R}(z-t)^+\,d\gamma(z)\right|\le C\varepsilon,\]
where $x$ is uniform on the sign cube and $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian measure.
hypotheses_covered: $a\in\mathbb R^n$ has squared coordinates summing to $1$
A single constant $C>0$ works for all such choices
